proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag varies over time or is shorter/longer than 2 weeks, the fixed delay can shift peaks and degrade timing; SEIRS may also over-attribute multi-wave structure to waning rather than reporting dynamics.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate target can plausibly lag infections; SEIRS captures waning immunity within-season and supports moderate peakiness while keeping the template parsimonious. A 2-week delay aligns with the stated surveillance semantics and prior discovered patterns.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning meaningfully shapes the curve, SEIR may underfit late-season persistence; if the true lag is closer to 2–3 weeks, peak timing may be early.
proposals.rationale: A simpler alternative to SEIRS when the 31-week training window does not strongly support estimating waning; 1-week delayed_I reflects near-term admission lag while retaining an exposed stage for influenza incubation.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H dynamics may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (e.g., I→H rate vs. H duration) and unstable forecasts, especially around the peak.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the observed hospitalization rate to an explicit hospitalized compartment, matching target semantics without an ad hoc delay. Useful as a mechanistically aligned comparator despite identifiability concerns.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true signal is closer to pure admissions, I+H can inflate early-season levels and blur peak shape; conversely, if H is negligible, the extra compartment may add unnecessary flexibility.
proposals.rationale: If surveillance captures a mixture of infectious burden and admissions (or if admissions are proportional to a combination of I and H), observing I+H can be a robust compromise that reduces sensitivity to H-only identifiability while still leveraging an H compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Fractional dynamics can over-smooth or introduce long-memory tails that misrepresent sharp changes; may be harder to distinguish from simple reporting lag effects in short series.
proposals.rationale: Fractional-order SEIRS can flexibly represent heterogeneous mixing and memory effects, which may help with high rate scale and moderate peakiness while keeping the observation aligned with plausible admission lag.
